# 0005 — Mask assets are generated by illuminator and shipped in the frontend bundle

- Status: Accepted
- Date: 2026-07-25

## Context

Masks are spatial-control material for the visualizer: inkblots, logos, silhouettes, and
hand-authored boundary shapes, converted at runtime into distance fields, gradient fields, and
stencils. They are a fixed visual library shared by every scene, not per-release metadata.

The catalog has no place for them and does not want one. Release artwork is a JSONB column on the
published-release tables, and RDS is the source of truth for catalog rows, so adding masks there
would mean migrations, admin CRUD, upload endpoints, and encode-adjacent plumbing for assets that
never vary by track.

Generation is handled by `../illuminator`, a batch image pipeline driven by a TOML pack whose
post-processor dispatches on asset type in `post/process.py`. Its type set covers sprites, hex
tiles, icons, card faces, chrome, backgrounds, and passthrough. A mask needs different treatment:
single-channel luminance output with explicit control over threshold and edge falloff, since
downstream distance-field generation depends on clean boundaries.

## Decision

A `mask` asset type is added to illuminator — union entry, allowed set, type resolution,
`process_mask`, and a type prompt fragment — and the generated masks are committed to
`frontend/public/masks/` alongside a manifest describing each mask's interpretation, symmetry, and
tiling behavior.

## Alternatives considered

- **Upload masks to the generated-media S3 bucket and serve them through the media CDN** — keeps
  binary assets out of Git and matches how artwork and audio are served. Requires a publish path,
  cache-invalidation handling, and a manifest fetched at runtime, all for assets that change only
  when the visual library is deliberately extended. Rejected as pipeline cost without benefit at
  this size; worth revisiting if the library outgrows the bundle.
- **Model masks as catalog entities in RDS with admin management** — enables per-release mask
  assignment and editing without a deploy. Costs a migration, API surface, admin UI, and a new
  asset kind, and encodes a per-track relationship that the design explicitly does not want, since
  masks must remain a global library the scheduler draws from. Rejected.
- **Author masks as procedural SDFs in shader code instead of images** — no assets at all, exact
  at every resolution, trivially cheap. Cannot express the organic, hand-authored, Rorschach-style
  shapes that motivate the feature. Rejected as a replacement; the SDF shape source covers the
  procedural case in parallel.
- **Generate masks by hand in an image editor** — no illuminator change needed. Loses batch
  consistency of style and palette across the library and the embedded provenance metadata used to
  audit how a mask was made. Rejected.

## Consequences

Masks are same-origin, so mask textures raise no cross-origin tainting question at all, and the
mask library is versioned with the code that consumes it. Collision and containment behavior
therefore does not silently change when a scene happens to select a given mask. Adding a mask is a
commit, with no runtime publish step.

Binary assets enter the repository and the frontend bundle, so the library's size is a build-size
concern, and extending it requires a deploy rather than an upload. Illuminator gains a type whose
only consumer is this repository, which is a cross-repository coupling to keep in view when its
asset-type set changes.
